stem: Two cultivars grown in the same room reach the same day of flowering, but their glandular trichome development differs. Which interpretation is best supported?
choices: Attribute the difference mainly to irrigation because plants at the same flowering age should otherwise show comparable trichome development
Use the shared flowering date as the harvest target because a common environment should minimize cultivar-specific maturity differences
Treat trichome development as genotype dependent and assess each cultivar with repeated representative observations before harvest
Assume the visual difference reflects sampling error unless environmental records show a separate treatment between the cultivars
rationale: Peer-reviewed evidence indicates that glandular trichome development and maturation can vary with genotype as well as plant age. Maturity decisions should therefore use cultivar-specific representative observations rather than a universal date.
